techniques_found.name: Super Learner / Stacked Generalization
techniques_found.source: Ensemble learning literature (e.g., 'Super Learner' by van der Laan et al., 2007)
techniques_found.expected_impact: Potential Brier score improvement of 0.005-0.010 by combining the strengths of diverse base models (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, ExtraTrees) and potentially reducing variance. Can outperform individual models.
techniques_found.implementation_notes: Train base models on k-folds of the training data. Use their out-of-fold predictions as features for a meta-learner (e.g., Logistic Regression, another simple GBM, or a neural net) trained on the full dataset. Ensure a proper hold-out set for final evaluation. This is inherently CPU-friendly if base and meta-learners are CPU-based.

techniques_found.name: Advanced Hyperparameter Optimization (HPO) with Optuna/Ray Tune
techniques_found.source: Optuna: 'Optuna: A Next-generation Hyperparameter Optimization Framework' (Akiba et al., 2019); Ray Tune: 'Ray Tune: A Distributed Hyperparameter Optimization Framework' (Li et al., 2019)
techniques_found.expected_impact: Potential Brier score improvement of 0.002-0.005 by finding significantly better hyperparameters for existing tree-based models, especially when considering interactions between parameters.
techniques_found.implementation_notes: Integrate Optuna (or Ray Tune for distributed HPO) with existing model training pipelines. Define search spaces for XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, etc., and optimize directly for Brier score or log-loss using walk-forward validation. Can leverage existing CPU resources efficiently.

techniques_found.name: Post-Hoc Probability Calibration (Platt Scaling, Isotonic Regression)
techniques_found.source: Predicting Good Probabilities With Supervised Learning (Platt, 1999); Isotonic Regression for Post-hoc Probability Calibration (Zadrozny & Elkan, 2002)
techniques_found.expected_impact: Crucial for Brier score targets. Can improve Brier by 0.003-0.007 if models are currently miscalibrated. Ensures predicted probabilities align with true event frequencies.
techniques_found.implementation_notes: Apply `sklearn.calibration.CalibratedClassifierCV` (using Platt Scaling or Isotonic Regression) to the raw probability outputs of the best performing or stacked models. Train the calibrator on a separate validation set or using cross-validation to prevent overfitting. This is a lightweight, CPU-friendly post-processing step.

techniques_found.name: Concept Drift Detection & Adaptive Ensembling
techniques_found.source: Machine Learning for Streaming Data with Concept Drift (Gama et al., 2014); ADWIN (Bifet et al., 2007)
techniques_found.expected_impact: Potential Brier score improvement of 0.005-0.010 by ensuring models remain relevant to the current NBA landscape, preventing performance degradation due to changes in team strategies, player rosters, or game rules over time.
techniques_found.implementation_notes: Monitor model performance (e.g., Brier score) and feature distributions over rolling time windows. Implement a mechanism (e.g., ADWIN or similar) to detect significant shifts. When drift is detected, trigger partial retraining, re-weighting of ensemble members, or re-run of the genetic algorithm for feature selection. Requires robust monitoring infrastructure and automated retraining pipelines.

feature_ideas.name: Advanced Player Impact Metrics
feature_ideas.description: Incorporate modern all-in-one player metrics that estimate individual player contributions to team success beyond traditional box score stats. Examples include RAPTOR (FiveThirtyEight), EPM (Estimated Plus/Minus), LEBRON (Luck-adjusted EPM by BBall-Index). These capture offensive and defensive value more robustly.
feature_ideas.data_source: Publicly available APIs/datasets (e.g., FiveThirtyEight, Dunks & Threes, BBall-Index) or derive similar metrics from play-by-play data.

feature_ideas.name: Schedule Congestion & Travel Logistics
feature_ideas.description: Features quantifying player/team fatigue and advantage/disadvantage due to schedule. Examples: number of games in the last N days, days since last game, back-to-back status, distance traveled for the current game, time zone changes.
feature_ideas.data_source: NBA official schedule data, team city locations, historical game logs.

feature_ideas.name: Injury Impact Quantification
feature_ideas.description: Beyond just a binary 'player injured' flag. Develop a method to estimate the 'value over replacement player' (VORP) loss due to key injuries, potentially by comparing the injured player's net rating/impact to that of their typical replacement.
feature_ideas.data_source: Injury reports (ESPN, official team reports), individual player advanced metrics, lineup data.

feature_ideas.name: Lineup Stability & Rotational Consistency
feature_ideas.description: Metrics reflecting how consistent a team's starting lineup and primary rotation players are. High turnover could indicate instability or adaptation, while stability often correlates with chemistry and efficiency.
feature_ideas.data_source: Official box scores, play-by-play data (to track minutes for non-starters).

calibration_insights: Systematic application of post-hoc calibration methods (Platt Scaling for models that output log-odds, Isotonic Regression for more flexible calibration) is critical. Apply these on the final predicted probabilities from the best single model or the stacked ensemble.

Monitor calibration regularly using reliability diagrams, Expected Calibration Error (ECE), and Maximum Calibration Error (MCE) on a dedicated hold-out set. This provides a visual and quantitative measure of how well predicted probabilities match true frequencies.

Ensure the loss function used during training for the tree ensembles (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) is appropriate for probabilistic prediction (e.g., 'binary:logistic' with logloss/cross-entropy). While Brier is the target, optimizing directly for it in tree models can be complex, and cross-entropy is a good proxy for well-calibrated probabilities.

For the TabICL neural model, experiment with temperature scaling as a simple and effective post-hoc calibration technique without requiring retraining. Optimize the single 'temperature' parameter on a validation set for Brier score.
recommended_next_action: Implement a robust stacking ensemble strategy combining existing tree models (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, ExtraTrees) with a simple meta-learner (e.g., Logistic Regression), followed by post-hoc calibration (Platt Scaling or Isotonic Regression) on the final stacked probabilities, using walk-forward validation for all training and calibration steps.
